reconstructed_theorem_text: For every positive integer n and every nonnegative integer h, let B be the set of pairs b = (i, p) of integers with 0 ≤ i ≤ h and p even, 4 ≤ p ≤ 2^(64(h + 1)). For each b = (i, p) in B, let C_b be the set of all functions from the triples (u, j, k) with 0 ≤ u < p, 0 ≤ j ≤ h − i, and 0 ≤ k < (2^(74(h + 1)))^j, to the integers {0, …, n − 1}. Let J be the disjoint union of the C_b indexed by B, so its elements are pairs (b, c) with c in C_b. Let P be the standard Gaussian measure on R^J. The map from R^J to the product of the spaces R^(C_b) that sends ξ to the family of blocks ((ξ_(b,c))_{c in C_b})_{b in B} is almost-everywhere measurable with respect to P, and its pushforward of P is the product over b in B of the standard Gaussian measures on R^(C_b).
objects: B is the block label type. C_b is the finite function type for the coordinates within block b, using the argument pair (u, (j, k)). J is the dependent sum of the C_b. The block map restricts ξ to the coordinates with label b and regards that same array as a Euclidean vector. P is the ambient standard Gaussian; the target measure is the product of the block standard Gaussians.
domains: n : ℕ+; h : ℕ; b = (i, p) in Fin(h + 1) × {p : Fin(2^(64(h + 1)) + 1) | p.val is even and p.val ≥ 4}. Within block b, u : Fin(p.val), j : Fin(h − i.val + 1), and k : Fin((2^(74(h + 1)))^(j.val)); every c in C_b maps each (u, (j, k)) to Fin(n.val). ξ is in EuclideanSpace ℝ J, and the output is in the dependent product of EuclideanSpace ℝ C_b over b in B.
quantifiers: The only outer quantifiers are ∀ n : ℕ+ and ∀ h : ℕ, in that order. B, the family C_b, and the block map are local definitions. The binders ξ and b define the block map; c defines its entries, and j indexes the dependent sum in each argument domain.
assumptions: There are no separate hypotheses beyond the outer binder types n : ℕ+ and h : ℕ. Evenness and the lower and upper bounds on p restrict block labels; the bounds on u, j, and k restrict arguments of the coordinate-indexing functions.
conclusion: The block map is almost-everywhere measurable for the standard Gaussian on EuclideanSpace ℝ J, and its pushforward of that measure is the product over b in B of the standard Gaussian on EuclideanSpace ℝ C_b. In particular, under that ambient measure the blocks are jointly independent and each has the stated standard Gaussian law.
scopes: All definitions and the law assertion are inside the scope of n and h. B depends on h; C_b depends on n, h, and b. In its dependent sum the range of j depends on h and i, and the range of k depends on h and j. Since i ≤ h, the natural subtraction h − i agrees with ordinary subtraction here. The map is defined on the entire ambient Euclidean space; almost-everywhere measurability and the pushforward equality are assertions relative to its standard Gaussian measure.
constant_dependencies: The label upper bound 2^(64(h + 1)) depends only on h, and the lower bound 4 and parity restriction are fixed. The inner base 2^(74(h + 1)) depends only on h; it is raised to j. The remaining sizes use p for u, h − i + 1 for j, and n for the function codomain. The Gaussian laws use the indicated real Euclidean coordinate spaces with identity covariance, without any free scale parameter.
